title: Segler, Preuss & Waller: Deep Neural Networks + Monte Carlo Tree Search Match Human Chemists in Organic Retrosynthesis
aiSystem: 3N-MCTS (Three Neural Networks + Monte Carlo Tree Search, Segler et al.)
whyItMatters: Published in Nature, 3N-MCTS ended 60 years of brittle rule-based synthesis planning by pairing deep policy/filter networks with MCTS—solving 2× more organic molecules 30× faster and tying human chemists in double-blind tests.
summary: Published in Nature on March 28, 2018, Marwin H. S. Segler, Mike Preuss, and Mark P. Waller at the University of Münster broke a 60-year bottleneck in computer-aided organic synthesis planning (dating back to E. J. Corey’s pioneering 1960s LHASA program). Trained on roughly 12 million published organic reactions, their 3N-MCTS neuro-symbolic system combined Monte Carlo Tree Search with three neural networks (an expansion policy, an in-scope reaction filter, and a rollout policy) to plan multi-step retrosynthetic routes autonomously. It solved nearly twice as many target molecules 30× faster than classical heuristic tools, and in a double-blind A/B evaluation, expert organic chemists judged its computer-generated routes equivalent in quality to published human literature syntheses.
technicalHighlights: Trained three deep neural networks on ~12 million published organic reactions and coupled them to symbolic Monte Carlo Tree Search (3N-MCTS).
Solved ~2× more organic target molecules 30× faster than classical rule-based retrosynthesis engines.
First automated synthesis planner whose routes were indistinguishable from human literature routes in a double-blind chemist evaluation.
caveats: Evaluated via double-blind route quality and benchmark solve rates rather than robotic wet-lab synthesis of every proposed route; stereochemistry and rare reaction conditions remained active follow-up challenges.

scoreRationale.foundational: Landmark neuro-symbolic breakthrough in chemistry—translating AlphaGo-style MCTS + neural policies to solve a 60-year grand challenge in organic retrosynthesis.
scoreRationale.ripple: Became the foundational paradigm for modern automated synthesis planning (AiZynthFinder, ASKCOS, Coscientist, robotic synthesis labs).
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (Vol. 555, pp. 604–610) with double-blind expert chemist evaluation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivered a 30× speedup over legacy computer-aided synthesis tools while doubling solvability.
